question: Which of the following methods is the quickest way to open an existing MS Excel spreadsheet?

options.text: Open MS Excel and click Blank Workbook
Double-click the .xlsx file in File Explorer

solution:
The Correct answer is __**Double-click the .xlsx file in File Explorer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Double-clicking a **.xlsx file** in **File Explorer** is the quickest method to open an existing **Excel spreadsheet**. This method bypasses the need to manually open the application and locate the file within the software.
 
• Excel files are identified by their **.xlsx extension**, which is the default format for spreadsheets created in **Microsoft Excel.**
 
• When double-clicked, the file automatically opens in **Microsoft Excel**, provided the software is installed and properly associated with the file type.
 
• This method is user-friendly and eliminates additional steps such as navigating through the **Excel interface** or using shortcuts.
 
• It is especially useful when working with files stored in specific folders or directories, ensuring faster access and convenience.
 
• The association between the **.xlsx file extension** and Microsoft Excel is set during the installation of the software, making this method seamless for most users.
 
• Double-clicking files is a universally recognized way to open documents in their designated applications across most **operating systems**, such as **Windows** and **macOS**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Open MS Excel and click Blank Workbook**__

 __
 
• This method is primarily used to create a **new spreadsheet**, not to open an existing file.
 
• While this approach allows users to access Excel, they would still need to manually locate and open the desired file.
 
• This process is slower compared to directly opening the file by double-clicking it.
 
 
 
• **Use the Alt + F4 shortcut**__
 __
 
• **Alt + F4** is a shortcut to close the currently active window, including Microsoft Excel.
 
• It is not used to open existing spreadsheets and is designed to exit or terminate applications.
 
• This shortcut is widely used for closing programs in **Windows operating systems**.
 
 
 
• **Press Ctrl + N**__
 
 
• **Ctrl + N** is a shortcut for creating a **new workbook** in Microsoft Excel, not opening an existing file.
 
• It is helpful for quickly starting a new project but would require additional steps to locate and open an existing spreadsheet.
 
• This shortcut is part of the broader range of **keyboard shortcuts** available in Excel.
